prompt: What is the difference between Comparable and Comparator in Java?
choices: Comparable is for primitives; Comparator is for objects
Comparable defines the class's own natural ordering; Comparator defines an external/alternate ordering
Comparable can only compare Strings; Comparator can compare any type
They are identical — Comparator extends Comparable
explanation: Comparable is implemented by the class itself (intrinsic ordering). Comparator is a separate object defining an alternate sort order — useful when you need multiple orderings (e.g., sort by name, then by age) or when you can't modify the class.
